newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says Airbus restructuring plan must go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says Airbus restructuring plan must go ahead.

text.p: European aircraft maker Airbus-Industrie must continue to restructure despite its improved orders position, Norbert Lammert, parliamentary state secretary to the German economics ministry, said.
Lammert told journalists on Friday evening in the east German town of Dessau that the German government was keen for the restructuring to go ahead despite the recent improvement.
In May, the four component parts of Airbus agreed under government pressure to pave the way for a single management structure for the whole company in a bid to cut back on costs.

Airbus is made up of Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace (dasa), France's Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace und Spain's CASA. The four companies are currently only loosely linked, creating some problems in decision-making.

Lammert said that plans to introduce a larger aircraft, with up to 600 seats, could only go ahead if the firms' structure were modified. Bonn continued to support this project, but only on condition that the reforms took place.

After a period of difficulty, Airbus has proved able to improve its sales figures considerably in the last few months. Orders included a commission for 120 aircraft from U.S. airline USAir with an option for a further 280 planes.
